A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the oxidative cyclization is favored by the electron-withdrawing character of the quinone moiety, the electron-donating character of the amine substituents, and the presence of the benzene ring in the 2-amino group.

oxidative cyclization of quinone imine derivatives to phenazinoid compounds is facilitated by (i) an electron-releasing group at the N-aryl fragment and (ii) an electron-repelling group at the N-heterocyclic fragment of the quinone imide.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the ease of the oxidative cyclization depends not only on the nature of the N-aryl substituent but also on the structure of the quinone imine fragment.
N-aryl groups are not necessary for the oxidative cyclization reaction to occur, but they can be used to fine-tune the reactivity.
